sections.html:
Logan County sits in central Illinois farm country, with Lincoln as the seat and the biggest city. Atlanta and Mount Pulaski are the other two cities. I-55 links Lincoln to Bloomington and Springfield, and Amtrak stops at Lincoln Station. The county covers roughly 618 square miles of land.

Winters are cold, with 126 days a year below freezing, so a buyer's inspector will look hard at the roof, gutters and foundation.

sections.h2: Which county offices handle your tax bill
sections.html:
Three Lincoln offices split the job.

  • Supervisor of Assessments (122 N. McLean St., 217-732-9635): directs the township assessors, keeps tax maps and parcel record cards, grants exemptions and serves as clerk to the Board of Review.
  • County Clerk (courthouse Room 20, 217-732-4148): applies each levy to the assessed base to produce rates, and handles redemption of tax sale certificates.
  • County Treasurer (courthouse Room 11, 217-732-3761): mails bills, takes payments, logs granted appeals and distributes the money.

The Treasurer also serves as county collector for real estate, mobile home and drainage tax. Every owner pays county, township and road and bridge tax. Schools, fire protection and other districts add to that, so your rate depends on which boundaries enclose your parcel.

Logan County bills a year behind, so tax collected in 2026 covers the 2025 tax year. The pattern repeats each year with new dates.

  • Real estate bills are mailed in May.
  • The first installment is due June 15 and the second September 1. Each carries a 1.5% monthly penalty if missed.
  • Mobile home bills go out at the end of March and are due June 1. After that day a $25 penalty applies, and another $25 is added each month, capped at $100.
  • The tax sale is held in the fall, with buyer registration closing about two weeks earlier.

Under Public Act 104-0553, Logan County chose to acquire delinquent real estate taxes as trustee for the taxing districts. If a due date has slipped by, phone the Treasurer for the current payoff, since the penalty keeps growing.

Bring the payment stub from your bill whichever way you pay. Choices:

  • The counter in courthouse Room 11, with cash or check. Cards work for real estate tax only, at 2.35% plus $1.50.
  • The drop box on N. Kickapoo St. facing Latham Park, or the boxes on the north and south sides of the courthouse. Do not put cash in the boxes.
  • Most banks in the county, except Regions and CEFCU.
  • Mail, where the postmark counts as the date received.
  • Card or e-check by phone at 217-203-8359 with your property index number, or through the link on the Treasurer's web page.

A bill you never received is still owed. A mailed payment is timely if postmarked by the due date, and the first installment is delinquent after the later of June 1 or the day after the printed date (35 ILCS 200/21-15).

sections.h2: How a Logan County bill is built
sections.html:
Township and county assessors set the assessed value. The abstract then goes to the state, which may apply a multiplier that lifts values, lowers them or leaves them alone. The County Clerk divides each district's levy by that district's assessed valuation to reach a rate, held to any statutory cap. Your tax is the combined rate times your equalized assessed value.

The assessment level is one-third of market value. The Supervisor of Assessments applies equalization factors to hold it there. Board of Review rules call for every parcel to be reassessed on a four-year cycle, though yearly reassessment is allowed. Each year's assessment changes are published in the Lincoln Courier.

The Supervisor also registers mobile homes. Taxes must be current and the title valid first, and you need a Treasurer's tax certificate to move a title at the Secretary of State.

You have 30 days from the publication of assessment changes in your township. Your complaint and evidence must reach the assessment office by 4:30 p.m. on the last day, or be mailed with a postmark on or before it. A chat with the assessor does not stop the clock.

A few rules trip people up:

  • One complaint per parcel, on the Board's own form. Faxed and emailed complaints are refused.
  • One copy of your evidence goes in with the form. A form that says no evidence provided will likely get a decision of no change.
  • Only the assessment can be protested, never the amount of tax.
  • If something is missing, you get a notice and 10 days to supply it.
  • Hearings are by appointment, last about 15 minutes, and take no new evidence.

Three members appointed by the County Board sit on the Board of Review, which convenes by the first Monday of June. You will get a written tentative decision, and you must ask for a hearing within the time printed on it.

The assessment office staff check eligibility and sometimes ask for proof every year. Exemptions on offer:

  • Owner-occupied homestead: $6,000 off assessed value if you live in the home you own.
  • Senior citizen: a further $5,000 once the owner reaches 65, with proof of age.
  • Senior freeze: holds the value at the first qualifying year for owners already on the senior exemption, with household gross income of $65,000 or less in assessment year 2025 and $75,000 or less from 2026.
  • Homestead improvement: shelters the added value from a garage, porch or deck on an owner-occupied house for four years.
  • Returning service members: $5,000 off the main residence for two straight years.
  • Service-connected disability: $2,500 at a 30 to 49% rating, $5,000 at 50 to 69%, and full exemption at 70% or above.
  • Persons with disabilities: $2,000, renewed with annual proof.

The first two amounts follow state law for a county that does not border one with 3,000,000 or more people (35 ILCS 200/15-175 and 15-170).

Look up your parcel on the county's tax search, compare it with the bill you hold, and phone the Treasurer for what is owed on any open installment. The title company splits the year between you and the buyer, and the settlement statement shows what is paid, due or held in escrow. A lender that escrows taxes can tell you what it has already sent.

Unpaid prior years make a sale harder. Ask the County Clerk whether the taxes were sold and what redemption costs, since a certificate holder must be paid before title is clear. The window is usually three years from the sale date, with exceptions (35 ILCS 200/21-350). A cash buyer can close on the payoff figures from those two offices, which keeps the timeline short when back taxes are involved.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Logan County Treasurer?
faqs.a: 217-732-3761. The office is in Room 11 of the courthouse in Lincoln, and that number is for bill questions and past-due amounts.

faqs.q: What is the late charge on Logan County real estate tax?
faqs.a: 1.5% per month is added when an installment is unpaid by its due date. Mobile home tax draws $25 after June 1, then $25 more each month up to $100.

faqs.q: Does the Logan County Treasurer accept cards?
faqs.a: Yes, for real estate tax. You can use the counter, the phone line at 217-203-8359 or the online link, and card payments at the counter carry a 2.35% plus $1.50 fee. Have your property index number ready.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for a Logan County assessment?
faqs.a: Thirty days from publication of changes for your township. The complaint and evidence must arrive by 4:30 p.m. or be postmarked by that day, and every parcel needs its own form.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for the homestead exemption in Logan County?
faqs.a: At the Supervisor of Assessments, 122 N. McLean St. in Lincoln, or by phone at 217-732-9635. The owner-occupied exemption takes $6,000 off assessed value.
